description: SQL query is built with an f-string from the raw customer value; a crafted name injects arbitrary SQL (find_orders_by_customer).
fix_hint: Use a parameterized query: conn.execute("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE customer LIKE ?", ("%" + customer + "%",)).

description: Billing API key is hardcoded in source (BILLING_API_KEY); credentials in code leak through VCS and builds.
fix_hint: Read the key from an environment variable or a secret store; fail fast when it is missing.

description: Bare `except:` in close_order swallows every error (including KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit), hiding webhook failures.
fix_hint: Catch the specific exceptions (e.g. urllib.error.URLError, OSError) and at minimum log the failure.

description: Mutable default argument tags=[] in create_order is shared between calls; appended values leak into later orders.
fix_hint: Use tags=None and `tags = list(tags) if tags else []` inside the function.

description: urllib.request.urlopen call in post_webhook has no timeout; a stalled webhook receiver hangs the caller forever.
fix_hint: Pass an explicit timeout (e.g. urlopen(req, timeout=10)) and handle the timeout error.

description: Discount-tier block in apply_discount is duplicated verbatim in legacy_report.report_discount; the two copies will drift.
fix_hint: Keep one implementation in billing.py and import it from the report module.

description: report_discount repeats the discount-tier block from billing.apply_discount line for line.
fix_hint: Delete the copy and call billing.apply_discount instead.

description: Magic numbers in tax logic (22, 1000000, 3500, 15000, 990) carry business meaning but have no names.
export_orders_xml returns None on its first statement; the XML-building body below is unreachable dead code.
fix_hint: Delete the function (and its callers, if any) or remove the early return if the export is still needed.

description: write_report opens the report file without a context manager and never closes it on the error path.
fix_hint: Wrap the writes in `with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:`.
